claims.statement: Adobe states that Service Account (JWT) credentials reached end of life on June 30, 2025 and are no longer supported; they cannot be created after June 3, 2024, and Adobe will convert remaining ones to OAuth Server-to-Server credentials after their certificates expire or on March 1, 2026, whichever is earlier.

sources.supports: As of June 30, 2025, Service Account (JWT) credentials have reached end of life; after June 3, 2024 no new ones can be created; automatic conversion after certificate expiry or March 1, 2026.
Notes that Service Account (JWT) credentials reached end of life and all server-to-server integrations must use OAuth Server-to-Server credentials.

claims.statement: The migration page contrasts the new credential with the Service Account (JWT) credential by saying the latter used a public certificate and private key pair to generate access tokens, that the developer downloaded and saved the private key, and that the pair had to be rotated every year.

sources.supports: The new credential does not use a public certificate and private key pair; you do not have to download and save the private key; the old credential needs the pair rotated every year.

claims.statement: Adobe's JWT documentation as archived on 2023-03-28 has the developer generate the private key and public certificate locally with an OpenSSL command that writes the key to a file named private.key and the certificate to certificate_pub.crt, and has the developer upload only the public certificate when creating the integration; the page states no encoding, prefix, header label or length for the private key file.

sources.supports: Create a private key and a public certificate. ... openssl req -x509 -sha256 -nodes -days 365 -newkey rsa:2048 -keyout private.key -out certificate_pub.crt
sources.locator: section "Create a Public Key Certificate", MacOS and Linux

sources.supports: Upload the public certificate (certificate_pub.crt) as a part of creating the integration.
sources.locator: section "Using the Public Key Certificate for Service Account Integration"

claims.statement: The archived 2023-03-28 JWT page states that the JWT must be signed with the private key of a digital signing certificate associated with the integration's API key, that the algorithm is RS256, and that the private key generates the signature while the Adobe Developer Console receives a public key to validate it.

sources.supports: The token must be signed using the private key for a digital signing certificate that is associated with your API key. ... RS256 (RSA Signature with SHA-256) is an asymmetric algorithm, and it uses a public/private key pair: the identity provider has a private (secret) key used to generate the signature, and the consumer of the JWT (i.e. Adobe Developer Console) gets a public key to validate the signature.

claims.statement: The archived 2023-03-28 JWT page lists three URL-encoded body parameters for the access-token exchange request to the IMS JWT exchange endpoint: client_id (the integration's API key), client_secret (the client secret generated for the integration) and jwt_token (a base-64 encoded JSON Web Token signed with a private key); the table lists no parameter that carries the private key itself.

sources.supports: client_id={api_key_value}&client_secret={client_secret_value}&jwt_token={base64_encoded_JWT}; jwt_token: A base-64 encoded JSON Web Token that encapsulates the identity of your integration, signed with a private key that corresponds to a public key certificate attached to the integration.
sources.locator: sections "Exchanging JWT to retrieve an access token" and "Request parameters"

claims.statement: The archived 2023-03-28 JWT page states the JWT's iss claim is the Organization ID in the format org_ident@AdobeOrg, its sub claim is the Technical Account ID in the format id@techacct.adobe.com, and its aud claim is the API key in the form https://ims-na1.adobelogin.com/c/api_key; these are identifiers carried in the JWT payload, not the private key.

sources.supports: iss: ... your Organization ID ... in the format org_ident@AdobeOrg. sub: ... your Technical Account ID ... in the format: id@techacct.adobe.com. aud: ... your API Key ... in the format: https://ims-na1.adobelogin.com/c/api_key.
sources.locator: section "Required Claims for a Service Account JWT"

claims.statement: The archived 2023-03-28 JWT page requires an exp claim and recommends a very short-lived JWT (a few minutes) that is signed and exchanged each time a new access token is needed, and discourages longer-lived JWTs that are reused to obtain access tokens.

sources.supports: Recommendation: Have a very short lived token (a few minutes) - such that it expires soon after it has been exchanged for an IMS access token. ... Longer lived tokens that are re-used to obtain access tokens as needed are not recommended.
sources.locator: section "Required Claims for a Service Account JWT", exp claim

claims.statement: Adobe's migration page as archived on 2023-05-31 (page footer 'Last updated 5/4/2023') states that applications using Service Account (JWT) credentials will stop working after Jan 1, 2025, shows a new Service Account (JWT) credential can be added for May 1, 2023 to Apr 30, 2024 and cannot be created or added from May 1, 2024, and shows Jan 1, 2025 as end of life.

sources.supports: Your applications using the Service Account (JWT) credentials will stop working after Jan 1, 2025. May 1, 2023 - Apr 30, 2024 / May 1, 2024 - Dec 31, 2024 / Jan 1, 2025 (end of life). A new Service Account (JWT) credential can be added to the project. A new Service Account (JWT) credential cannot be created or added to the project.
sources.locator: section "Deperecation Timelines" (spelled so on the page)

claims.statement: Adobe's migration page as archived on 2024-09-21 (page footer 'Last updated 4/4/2024') states that applications using Service Account (JWT) credentials will stop working after Jan 27, 2025 and shows the phases May 1, 2023 - Jun 2, 2024 and Jun 3, 2024 onward with Jan 27, 2025 as end of life.

sources.supports: Your applications using the Service Account (JWT) credentials will stop working after Jan 27, 2025. May 1, 2023 - Jun 2, 2024 / Jun 3, 2024 - Jan 26, 2024 / Jan 27, 2025 (end of life).
sources.locator: section "Deperecation Timelines" (spelled so on the page; the second range is printed with the year 2024 as shown)

claims.statement: Adobe's migration page as archived on 2025-03-28 states that the end-of-life date was extended from Jan 27, 2025 to Jun 30, 2025, that Adobe announced the deprecation on May 1, 2023, that after June 3, 2024 new Service Account (JWT) credentials cannot be created, that after June 30, 2025 certificates cannot be refreshed so integrations stop working once existing certificates expire, and that Adobe will convert remaining credentials to OAuth Server-to-Server credentials when certificates expire or on March 1, 2026, whichever comes first.

sources.supports: The end of life date for Service Account (JWT) credentials has been extended from Jan 27, 2025, to Jun 30, 2025, to give customers more time to migrate.

May 1, 2023 Adobe announces the deprecation of Service Account (JWT) credentials. ... June 3, 2024 After June 3, 2024, you cannot create new Service Account (JWT) credentials. June 30, 2025 (End of Life) After June 30, 2025, you cannot refresh certificates ... Your integrations will stop working once existing certificates expire. ... automatically convert ... when certificates expire or on March 1, 2026, whichever comes first.
sources.locator: section "Deperecation Timelines" (spelled so on the page)

claims.statement: Across three archived captures of one Adobe migration page, the stated end-of-life date for Service Account (JWT) credentials is Jan 1, 2025 (captured 2023-05-31), Jan 27, 2025 (captured 2024-09-21) and Jun 30, 2025 (captured 2025-03-28), and the stated date after which new credentials cannot be created moves from May 1, 2024 to Jun 3, 2024; the dates are announcements that the provider revised, so none of them is treated as a fixed interval during which a private key was valid.

sources.supports: Jan 1, 2025 (end of life); May 1, 2024 - Dec 31, 2024 phase: a new credential cannot be created or added.
extended from Jan 27, 2025, to Jun 30, 2025; June 3, 2024: After June 3, 2024, you cannot create new Service Account (JWT) credentials.

openQuestions.question: Adobe documentation read for this candidate gives no prefix, alphabet, length or other format rule for this value; any example in it is a placeholder or a public identifier. Not researched beyond existence.

This is a deprecated credential type. Whether private keys from it still exist in the wild, what encoding they use, and whether any still authenticate after the stated conversion dates are not established by the pages read; a historical contract would need a durable pin of the then-current documentation. Not assumed current.

The archived Adobe pages read give the private key's file name (private.key), generator (an OpenSSL command with rsa:2048) and use (RS256 signing), but no encoding (PEM, DER, PKCS#1 or PKCS#8), header label, length or any Adobe-specific marker. What a given OpenSSL version writes is a property of that tool, not an Adobe statement, and is not recorded as a claim. An Adobe statement or a dated capture of Adobe's own key-generation instructions naming the encoding would settle it.

Because the key is generated locally by a general-purpose tool and uploaded to nobody (only the certificate is uploaded), the pages read give nothing that makes the private key an Adobe-specific format. Whether an Adobe-specific carrier or marker for it exists is unresolved; this family therefore models a role (the signing half of the retired Service Account (JWT) credential), not a distinct grammar.

None of the pages read states when the Service Account (JWT) credential, or its certificate-based key pair, was introduced; the earliest dated statement read is the 2023-05-01 announcement of deprecation. Introduction is unknown, not assumed.

The provider states dates for announcement, the end of creation, end of life, certificate-expiry-bound failure and automatic conversion (no later than March 1, 2026 per the page read on 2026-10-05). It states no date on which a given JWT exchange last succeeded, and that date depends on each certificate's expiry. Whether any signed JWT is still accepted is not tested (no live verification) and is not established; an old private key found in logs or configuration is still a private key.

The JWT assertion is derived from the private key and is short-lived by recommendation, but the pages read state no maximum lifetime Adobe enforces, so a captured JWT is not recorded as expired or harmless. The client_secret that travels beside it in the exchange request is a separate credential outside this family.
